title: CatchUp! Capturing and replaying refactorings to support API evolution
authors: Johannes Henkel, Amer Diwan
central_claim: Records refactorings applied to a library and replays them on client code to migrate it to the new version.
cite_claim: Early client-adaptation tools replayed recorded library refactorings on clients. [verify: full text not opened; existence via S2 metadata, description via Dig & Johnson 2005 Sec. 1]
quote: CatchUp [13] is a tool that uses descriptions of refactorings to help application developers migrate their applications to a new version of a library.
relevance: Foundational root of the lineage; trigger is a known refactoring log, i.e., signature change.

title: The Role of Refactorings in API Evolution
authors: Danny Dig, Ralph E. Johnson
central_claim: Over 80% of API-breaking changes in Eclipse, Mortgage, Struts and log4j are refactorings; behavioural modifications compile but behave differently.
cite_claim: Refactorings dominated API-breaking changes in early Java framework studies, which motivated replay-based migration tools; behavioural changes were recognised but left out.
quote: Over 80% of these changes are refactorings.
relevance: Explains why the classic lineage targets structural breaks; Sec. 2 defines the behavioural class fiks targets ('might compile fine but behave differently at run time').

title: Recommending Adaptive Changes for Framework Evolution (SemDiff)
authors: Barthelemy Dagenais, Martin P. Robillard
central_claim: Recommends client adaptations by analysing how the framework adapted to its own changes; relevant replacement for 89% of broken calls (Eclipse JDT, 3 clients).
cite_claim: SemDiff takes calls to methods that no longer exist and recommends replacements mined from the framework's own history.
quote: Our study showed that our approach provided a relevant functionality replacement for 89% of the broken methods
relevance: Trigger is a broken call (compile-level); oracle is manual relevance. Shows the 'learn from upstream evidence' idea that fiks cannot use (no upstream history for a remote API).

title: A graph-based approach to API usage adaptation (LibSync)
authors: Hoan Anh Nguyen, Tung Thanh Nguyen, Gary Wilson Jr., Anh Tuan Nguyen, Miryung Kim, Tien N. Nguyen
central_claim: Learns API usage adaptation patterns from clients that already migrated and recommends edits to other clients.
cite_claim: Usage adaptation can be learned from already-migrated clients. [verify: abstract/full text not read; metadata only]
quote: [verify] no quote: abstract unavailable
relevance: Lineage step: client-to-client transfer of adaptations.

title: Meditor: Inference and Application of API Migration Edits
authors: Shengzhe Xu, Ziqi Dong, Na Meng
central_claim: Mines migration-related commits from 602,249 GitHub projects, infers 1,368 migration edits, applies them correctly in 218 of 225 cases.
cite_claim: Pattern-mined migration edits can be applied to clients with high precision when the migration is known.
quote: Our evaluation shows that Meditor correctly applied code migrations in 218 out of 225 cases.
relevance: Trigger = known library version migration; no runtime oracle.

title: A3: Assisting Android API Migrations Using Code Examples
authors: Maxime Lamothe, Weiyi Shang, Tse-Hsun (Peter) Chen
central_claim: Learns Android API migration patterns from code examples and assists migration in 71 of 80 cases; user study shows 29% time reduction.
cite_claim: Example-mined migration patterns assisted 71 of 80 Android API migrations.
quote: provide API migration assistance in 71 out of 80 cases
relevance: Lineage; 'what to migrate' assumed known from docs, unlike silent drift.

title: Automated API-usage update for Android apps (AppEvolve)
authors: Mattia Fazzini, Qi Xin, Alessandro Orso
central_claim: Updates Android apps for API changes using examples of how other developers evolved their apps for the same changes.
cite_claim: Given information about the API change, AppEvolve transfers other developers' updates to a target app.
quote: automatically perform app updates for API changes based on examples of how other developers evolved their apps for the same changes
relevance: Trigger = known API change information; example-driven.

title: AndroEvolve: Automated Android API Update with Data Flow Analysis and Variable Denormalization
authors: Stefanus A. Haryono, Ferdian Thung, David Lo, Lingxiao Jiang, Julia Lawall, Hong Jin Kang, Lucas Serrano, Gilles Muller
central_claim: Improves CocciEvolve deprecated-API updates with data-flow analysis and denormalisation: 26.90% more correct updates on 360 target files.
cite_claim: Deprecated-API update tools improved correctness over CocciEvolve by 26.90% on 360 files.
quote: AndroEvolve produces 26.90% more instances of correct updates compared to CocciEvolve.
relevance: Trigger = deprecation list; oracle not stated in abstract.

title: PCART: Automated Repair of Python API Parameter Compatibility Issues
authors: Shuai Zhang, Guanping Xiao, Jun Wang, Huashan Lei, Gangqiang He, Yepang Liu, Zheng Zheng
central_claim: Detects and repairs Python API parameter compatibility issues; F1 96.51% detection and 91.97% repair precision on PCBench (47,478 cases).
cite_claim: Signature-level Python API parameter changes can be repaired automatically with high precision.
quote: achieving an F1-score of 96.51% in detecting API parameter compatibility issues and a repair precision of 91.97%
relevance: Shows the signature-change sub-problem is largely solved; fiks's class is not signature changes.

title: Automated Update of Android Deprecated API Usages With Large Language Models (GUPPY)
authors: Tarek Mahmud, Bin Duan, Meiru Che, Awatif Yasmin, Anne H. H. Ngu, Guowei Yang
central_claim: GPT-4 updates deprecated Android API usages, generates tests, and iterates until tests pass; evaluated on 360 + 156 usages.
cite_claim: LLM-based API update loops can generate their own tests as the acceptance oracle.
quote: uses GPT-4 to generate tests, identify incorrect updates, and refine the API usage through an iterative process until the tests pass
relevance: Closest prior art for 'generate the test, then repair'; tests are LLM-generated, not derived from a runtime violation.

title: A Systematic Review of API Evolution Literature
authors: Maxime Lamothe, Yann-Gael Gueheneuc, Weiyi Shang
central_claim: SLR of API evolution; remaining challenges include drivers of API change, uniform benchmarks, and impact on API users.
cite_claim: A 2021 review lists uniform benchmarks and impact on API users among open API-evolution challenges.
quote: (2) creating and using uniform benchmarks for research evaluation
relevance: Survey anchor for the related-work paragraph.

title: Why and How Java Developers Break APIs
authors: Aline Brito, Laerte Xavier, Andre Hora, Marco Tulio Valente
central_claim: Firehouse field study over ~4 months of 400 Java libraries: 59 breaking changes confirmed by developers of 19 projects; motivations are new features, API simplification, maintainability.
cite_claim: Developers break APIs mainly to add features, simplify the API and improve maintainability. [verify exact abstract wording]
quote: [verify] paraphrase only: main motivations are implementing new features, simplifying APIs, improving maintainability
relevance: Motivation for why provider drift is deliberate and recurring.

title: BUMP: A Benchmark of Reproducible Breaking Dependency Updates
authors: Frank Reyes, Yogya Gamage, Gabriel Skoglund, Benoit Baudry, Martin Monperrus
central_claim: 571 breaking dependency updates from 153 Maven projects, each as a Docker image pair; failures: 243 compilation, 188 test, 121 enforcer, 14 lock, 5 resolution; 60 assertion failures.
cite_claim: In a compile/test-gated benchmark of breaking updates, assertion-level behavioural failures are a minority (60 of 571).
location: Def. 2-3; Table II; Table V; Sec. II-E
quote: BUMP contains 571 breaking dependency updates collected from 153 Java projects.
relevance: Reference substrate; its selection (build must fail) excludes silent drift by construction.

title: Breaking-Good: Explaining Breaking Dependency Updates with Build Analysis
authors: Frank Reyes, Benoit Baudry, Martin Monperrus
central_claim: Generates explanations for breaking updates from build logs; correct root cause for 70% of 243 breaking updates.
cite_claim: Build-log analysis explains 70% of compile-breaking dependency updates.
quote: Breaking-Good accurately identifies root causes and generates automatic explanations for 70% of these breaking updates.
relevance: Explanation analogue of fiks's receipt, but driven by build logs.

title: Byam: Fixing Breaking Dependency Updates with Large Language Models
authors: Frank Reyes, May Mahmoud, Federico Bono, Sarah Nadi, Benoit Baudry, Martin Monperrus
venue_or_publisher: arXiv:2505.07522 v3 (Feb 2026); S2 lists Empirical Software Engineering [verify venue]
central_claim: Compile-error-triggered LLM repair of client code on 103 BUMP cases; o3-mini fully repairs 27% of builds (28/103) and 78% of errors (741/955).
cite_claim: LLM repair of dependency-induced compilation errors fully fixes about a quarter of builds; behavioural failures are out of scope.
quote: We focus on breaking dependency updates that lead to compilation errors.
relevance: Strongest compile-triggered baseline; its trigger never fires on D1-D5.

title: Automatically Fixing Dependency Breaking Changes
authors: Lukas Fruntke, Jens Krinke
central_claim: Agentic and recursive zero-shot LLM repair on BUMP; test-suite repair success up to 23% (agentic) and 19% (zero-shot).
cite_claim: Agentic LLM repair of breaking dependency updates reaches up to 23% test-suite success on BUMP.
quote: the agentic approach achieving a repair success rate of up to 23%
relevance: Low-end success estimate under a test-suite oracle.

title: The Fix Is Right at Hand: Fixing Incompatibility Errors Guided by Library Knowledge for Automatic Library Upgrade (Librarian)
authors: Zhuotong Zhou et al.
central_claim: Extracts context-aware fix hints from the library codebase and refines with compilation feedback; 84.2% fixing success.
cite_claim: Library-knowledge-guided LLM repair with compile feedback reaches 84.2% fix success on incompatibility errors.
quote: Librarian achieves a fixing success rate of 84.2%, outperforming the state-of-the-arts by at least 45.3%
relevance: Shows upstream knowledge drives high success; fiks has none for a remote API.

title: Agentic Generation of AST Transformation Rules for Fixing Breaking Updates (BigBag)
authors: Frank Reyes, Benoit Baudry, Martin Monperrus
central_claim: Agent generates reusable AST transformations; 94.3% compilable, 78.6% fix rate on 157 compile-failure BUMP cases; 33.3% cross-project fix rate.
cite_claim: Repairs for one library update can be generalised into transformations that transfer across clients.
quote: The best configuration achieves a compilable transformation rate of 94.3% and a fix rate of 78.6%.
relevance: Analogue of 'fix once for every agent'; fiks fixes the shared tool rather than each client.

title: DepRepair: LLM-Based Source-Code Repair for Dependency Breaking Changes
authors: Shenghao Yang, Bo Lu, Yao Liu, Yu Kang, Qiongfang Zhang, Chetan Bansal, Saravan Rajmohan
central_claim: DepBench (95 instances, 4 ecosystems, Docker oracle running consumer tests); structured upstream evidence gives 89.5% (GPT-5.5); raw evidence lowers pass rates by 7-23 pp.
cite_claim: In dependency repair, structured upstream evidence raises LLM pass rates while raw evidence lowers them by 7-23 points; no failing test localises the break.
quote: no failing test localizes where the consumer breaks
relevance: Supports H-CA3 (structured evidence helps); its evidence source (release notes, API diff) is absent in fiks's setting.

title: Break to Adapt: Knowledge-Based Updates of Breaking Dependencies in JavaScript (BDUpdater)
authors: Yifan Xia, Chengwei Liu, Zifan Xie, Lyuye Zhang, Peiyu Liu, Kangjie Lu, Yang Liu
central_claim: Without compile errors (JavaScript), mined breaking-change records guide LLM migration; 90.5% of breaking updates recovered across 84 clients at about $0.05 each.
cite_claim: In dynamic languages, which have no compile oracle, mined change records substitute for compiler feedback.
quote: recovers 90.5% of the breaking dependency updates with high semantic equivalence to developer-authored adaptations
relevance: Shows the compile-trigger assumption breaks in JS; still relies on provider-written change records.

title: DependaFix: A GitHub App for Fixing Breaking Dependency Updates in CI Build for Java Projects
authors: Enock Mecheo, May Mahmoud, Sarah Nadi
central_claim: GitHub App that detects failing dependency-update PRs, extracts CI context, delegates to Byam, and opens a repair PR if the fix succeeds.
cite_claim: Breaking-update repair has been integrated into GitHub CI as an app that opens repair pull requests.
quote: creates a pull request for the repair if the fix succeeds
relevance: Closest 'ship a PR' analogue; trigger is a failing dependency-bump PR, which never exists for server-side drift.

title: Taming Behavioral Backward Incompatibilities via Cross-Project Testing and Analysis (DeBBI)
authors: Lingchao Chen, Foyzul Hassan, Xiaoyin Wang, Lingming Zhang
central_claim: Library regression suites miss behavioural backward incompatibilities; cross-project testing with client tests exposes them.
cite_claim: Library-side regression tests often fail to detect behavioural backward incompatibilities.
quote: the regression test suites of library projects often fail to detect all BBIs
relevance: Behavioural detection line; detection only.

title: Can We Trust Tests To Automate Dependency Updates? A Case Study of Java Projects
authors: Joseph Hejderup, Georgios Gousios
venue_or_publisher: Journal of Systems and Software (2022); arXiv:2109.11921
central_claim: Tests cover 58% of direct and 20% of transitive dependency calls and detect 47%/35% of injected faults; change impact analysis detects 74%/64%.
cite_claim: Client test suites detect fewer than half of injected semantic faults in direct dependencies, so test-gated update bots miss behavioural breaks.
quote: tests can only detect 47% of direct and 35% of indirect artificial faults on average
relevance: Key evidence that test-triggered pipelines under-fire on behavioural drift (supports H-CA2).

title: Using Others' Tests to Identify Breaking Updates
authors: Suhaib Mujahid, Rabe Abdalkareem, Emad Shihab, Shane McIntosh
central_claim: Uses test suites of other dependents of the same package to detect breakage-inducing npm versions (391,553 packages).
cite_claim: Crowd client tests broaden the usage scenarios against which a new version is checked.
quote: leverage the automated test suites of other projects that depend upon the same dependency to test newly released versions
relevance: Analogue of fiks's 'real traffic as test oracle' idea, at the library level.

title: Compsuite: A Dataset of Java Library Upgrade Incompatibility Issues
authors: Xiufeng Xu, Chenguang Zhu, Yi Li
central_claim: 123 real Java client-library incompatibilities, each with a developer-authored reproducing test and a CLI.
cite_claim: Real upgrade incompatibilities come with developer tests that reproduce them.
quote: Each incompatibility issue in Compsuite is associated with a test case authored by the developers
relevance: Possible external behavioural substrate (Java).

title: Client-Library Compatibility Testing with API Interaction Snapshots (Gilesi)
authors: Gustave Monce, Thomas Degueule, Jean-Remy Falleri, Romain Robbes
central_claim: Records API interactions at the client-library boundary during client tests and diffs the snapshots across versions; kills ~96% vs ~89% of 158 extreme mutants; detection only.
cite_claim: Recorded client-library interaction snapshots can act as an oracle for behavioural breaking changes that client assertions miss.
location: Sec. III-A, III-C; Sec. IV-B, Table I
quote: Any difference between the original and the new snapshots indicates a change in the library's behavior.
relevance: Strongest contract-free detection competitor (H-CA6); no repair, no noise/FP study.

title: Who Broke Me? Execution-Guided Repair of Behavioral Dependency Breaks (BBCFixer)
authors: Juntao Chen, Tingting Bi, Yanlin Wang, Patanamon Thongtanunam
central_claim: Repairs interface-preserving behavioural breaks by running the failing test under old and new library, localising the first divergent API call; BBCBench (41 Py + 59 JS); 58.0 vs 49.7 pure agent (qwen3-coder).
cite_claim: Execution-guided localisation of behavioural dependency breaks improves agent repair over a pure agent; the oracle (reference tests) is an upper bound on correctness.
location: Sec. 1; Sec. 3.1; Sec. 3.2.3; Table 1; Table 4; Sec. 6
quote: the interface remains intact, but the run-time behavior changes
relevance: Closest prior work to fiks's repair stage; requires a failing test and a re-executable old version, which fiks does not have.

title: Update from Hell: Can Coding Agents Survive Hidden Breakage in Dependency Upgrades?
authors: Zijian Luo, Runzhi He, Pengfei Gao, Yu Kang, Zeqi Lin, Minghua Ma, Qingwei Lin, Saravan Rajmohan, Yongqiang Tian
central_claim: DepBench: 203 upgrade tasks mined from Dependabot/Renovate PRs across 5 ecosystems with hidden post-upgrade tests; best 104/203; in 61.8% of failures visible tests passed.
cite_claim: Coding agents often pass visible tests while missing upgrade-induced behaviour changes, so visible-test success is not evidence of a complete repair.
location: Sec. II; Table II; Sec. IV-E, Table VIII
quote: satisfy the old visible test surface but miss the dependency-upgrade behavior
relevance: Motivates fiks's property-specific repro and hidden-test evaluation (H-CA4).

title: MigrationBench: Repository-Level Code Migration Benchmark from Java 8
authors: Linbo Liu, Xinle Liu, Qiang Zhou, Lin Chen, Yihan Liu, Hoan Nguyen, Behrooz Omidvar-Tehrani, Xi Shen, Jun Huan, Omer Tripp, Anoop Deoras
central_claim: 5,102 repos (300 selected) for Java 8 to 17/21; agentic Claude-4.5-Sonnet reaches 71.67% minimal and 53.33% maximal pass@1; compile-only checking inflates minimal success to 97.67%.
cite_claim: Migration success measured by compilation alone greatly overstates success measured by tests that cannot be deleted or renamed.
quote: passes all existing unit and integration tests
relevance: Oracle-design lesson (anti-reward-hacking rules r3/r4) that fiks's gate should mirror.

title: An Empirical Study of Python Library Migration Using Large Language Models
authors: Md Mohayeminul Islam, Ajay Kumar Jha, May Mahmoud, Ildar Akhmetov, Sarah Nadi
central_claim: On PyMigBench, GPT-4o migrates 94% of code changes correctly, but only 64% (16 of 25) of test-evaluated migrations pass the developers' tests.
cite_claim: LLM migrations that look correct change by change often fail the project's tests.
location: Table II (Sec. IV-C1); Table IV (Sec. V-B)
quote: 4o performs best, with 94% of the code changes being correct.
relevance: Gap between edit-level and run-time correctness.

title: Pig: Leveraging Large Language Models for Python Library Migrations
authors: Miryeong Kang, Wonseok Oh, Gabin An, Hakjoo Oh
central_claim: API-level slicing and failure-pattern-aware prompting improve LLM Python library migration by 53.5% over baseline across 7 LLMs on 364 tasks.
cite_claim: Decomposing migrations into API-level slices improves LLM migration success.
quote: improves the average success rate of the baseline approach by 53.5% across seven different LLM models
relevance: Library-replacement migration; context only.

title: Migrating Code At Scale With LLMs At Google
authors: Celal Ziftci, Stoyan Nikolov, Anna Sjovall, Bo Kim, Daniele Codecasa, Max Kim
central_claim: Industrial report of an LLM-based automated algorithm for a large, traditionally manual migration at Google.
cite_claim: LLM-driven migrations are used in industry at scale with human review. [verify: results section not read]
quote: Migration is a common and typically continuous maintenance task undertaken either manually or through tooling.
relevance: Industry precedent for LLM changes landing via human-reviewed changes.

title: GitChameleon: Evaluating AI Code Generation Against Python Library Version Incompatibilities
authors: Diganta Misra, Nizar Islah, Victor May, Brice Rauby, Zihan Wang, Justine Gehring et al.
central_claim: 328 version-conditioned Python completion problems with executable tests; evaluates LLMs, agents, assistants and RAG.
cite_claim: Version-conditioned code generation remains hard for current LLMs and agents, measured by execution.
quote: comprising 328 Python code completion problems, each conditioned on specific library versions and accompanied by executable unit tests
relevance: Knowledge-update baseline family; scores model knowledge, not repair of a deployed wrapper.

title: Automating Dependency Updates in Practice: An Exploratory Study on GitHub Dependabot
authors: Runzhi He, Hao He, Yuxia Zhang, Minghui Zhou
central_claim: Dependabot reduces technical lag, but compatibility scores are too scarce to reduce update suspicion; 11.3% of projects abandoned it.
cite_claim: Developers distrust automated dependency PRs because compatibility signals are scarce.
quote: its compatibility scores are too scarce to be effective in reducing update suspicion
relevance: Bot-PR trust context for fiks's never-merge and green-CI policy.

title: Leveraging the Crowd for Dependency Management: An Empirical Study on the Dependabot Compatibility Score
authors: Benjamin Rombaut, Filipe R. Cogo, Ahmed E. Hassan
central_claim: Across 579,206 Dependabot PRs, a compatibility score cannot be computed for 83% of updates.
cite_claim: Crowd compatibility signals are unavailable for most dependency updates.
quote: a compatibility score cannot be calculated for 83% of the dependency updates due to the lack of data from the crowd
relevance: Industry-bot oracle weakness.

title: VulnBump: A Benchmark for Fixing Vulnerable Dependencies in Real Projects While Keeping the Build and Tests Green
authors: Gabija Pasiunaite, R. McMorrow, Brian Clark, Liran Tal, Luke Tu
central_claim: 307 vulnerability-driven upgrade tasks; pass requires fix + build + all previously passing tests; agents pass 59.6-90.2%, a non-agentic baseline 46.9%.
cite_claim: Remediation quality in dependency upgrades must be verified on fix, build and tests together.
quote: evaluating remediation quality in dependency upgrades requires verifying the fix, the build and the tests together
relevance: Supports multi-part gate design; industry (Snyk) agent comparison.

title: Skill Drift Is Contract Violation: Proactive Maintenance for LLM Agent Skill Libraries (SkillGuard)
authors: Linfeng Fan, Yuan Tian, Ziwei Li, Zhiwu Lu
central_claim: Treats agent-skill decay under external service/API change as contract violation; 0 false alarms on 599 negatives; 100% precision / 76% recall on known drift; repair 10% -> 78% with contract localisation.
cite_claim: Framing external drift as contract violation gives precise detection and lifts one-round repair from 10% to 78%.
quote: raises zero false alarms over 599 no-drift and hard-negative cases
relevance: Closest agent-era analogue: contracts + localised repair, but for skill documents, literal-verifier oracle, no PRs.
